correctness.rationale: The exact adjacency identity A^3=mn A gives U(t)=I+(cos(sqrt(mn)t)-1)A^2/(mn)+i sin(sqrt(mn)t)A/sqrt(mn). Hence every cross entry is (1-X^2)/(mn), and within-part off diagonals are (1-X)^2 divided by the part size squared. For m,n>=2 the necessary mn<=m+n forces m=n=2. For a star K_{1,n}, the hub diagonal and distinct leaf off-diagonal force E[X^2]=1/(n+1), E[X]=-(n-2)/2. n>=5 violates X>=-1; n=4 forces X=-1 almost surely, contradicting its second moment. Explicit probability laws realize each of four remaining types. For K_{1,4}, combining hub/leaf error inequalities with E[(1+X)^2]>=0 gives max entrywise error >=2/45. The proof covers arbitrary Borel sampling measures. Exact stdlib checks confirm 225 matrix families, four witnesses and 1445 sampled rational two-point laws. Finite checks are only corroboration; the algebra is unrestricted.

originality.rationale: Baptista--Coutinho--Marques, arXiv:2308.16378v1 Section 3.1 Proposition 9, eliminates only m+n>7 and states four affirmative examples, leaving the other low-order bicliques unclassified. The new argument eliminates all missing cases for any common probability law and gives an explicit K_{1,4} distance bound. Carlson et al., arXiv:quant-ph/0608044v1, analyze weight-varying and fixed-start instantaneous/long-time mixing rather than one fixed unweighted full mixing matrix averaged over an arbitrary common law. No dominating theorem was identified from the actual public-record and mathematically-focused searches, although literature indexing and publisher text access leave a residual risk.

value.rationale: The source investigates arbitrary-time sampling and explicitly stops at a coarse cutoff for complete bipartite graphs while listing positive low-order cases. The finding completes that natural structural classification at all graph sizes and for every time distribution, with a transparent exact reason why averaging cannot repair K1,4, K2,3 and other failures. Its sharp domain and simultaneous all-start quantifier matter for quantum-walk mixing protocols; the quantitative 2/45 gap further proves a robust boundary. Positive examples are credited, the K1,4 error bound is not claimed optimal, and the contribution is limited to bicliques.
